multiplayerRoom.syncInterrupted: {detail} Live updates are interrupted. Checking shared room state every two seconds; controls remain available when the room API is reachable.
multiplayerRoom.connectionInterrupted: Connection interrupted. Retrying; room controls are paused.
multiplayerRoom.syncReconnecting: Live updates are reconnecting. Checking shared room state every two seconds; controls remain available when the room API is reachable.
multiplayerRoom.noPreviousRoom: No previous room in this browser. Create or join one below.
multiplayerRoom.intro: Work through DNS and DHCP incidents together. Each responder discovers part of the evidence. Share your findings by voice or chat while you play.
multiplayerRoom.scoringRules: Team decisions score once when the host continues: 100 × streak (maximum ×3) for a clean decision; 50 if the team finds the correct answer with mistakes. Individual contributions are separate. Each distinct incorrect decision costs 5% uptime and 5 seconds; you can recover by choosing a different decision. Correct decisions earn +100 once. No speed bonus. A shared hint costs 25 team points.
multiplayerRoom.contributions: Evidence {evidence} · Correct answers {answers} · Role actions {actions} · Resolution {resolution}
multiplayerRoom.allReady: All connected players are ready. The host can start.
multiplayerRoom.notAllReady: Every connected player must mark ready. The host can exclude disconnected players after the absence threshold.
multiplayerRoom.recoveryExcluded: Disconnected for at least {seconds} seconds: {names}. These players will be excluded from this mission’s decisions and evidence requirements.
multiplayerRoom.recoveryRejoin: If they reconnect after the start, they can observe findings and the debrief with their identity and contributions preserved. A new room is needed to participate.
multiplayerRoom.recoveryUnready: Connected players still need to mark ready: {names}.
multiplayerRoom.observingMission: You are observing this mission after lobby recovery. Your identity and contributions are preserved. You have no required evidence (Complete · 0/0); follow shared findings and the debrief. Join a new room to participate.
multiplayerRoom.lobbyBody: Share code {code}. Tackle {count} incidents with a ten-minute discussion window per incident. Roles rotate after each incident. A solo responder receives all evidence; teams receive complementary clues to discuss. Rooms expire 30 minutes after creation.
multiplayerRoom.fallbackWait: Continue with current evidence becomes available in {seconds}s.
multiplayerRoom.fallbackReady: The timeout has elapsed. Continue even if your evidence card or a teammate is missing; this unlocks answers for this question without awarding discovery points.
multiplayerRoom.discoverBody: Discover and discuss each required evidence item. Teammates with the same item can cover for one another. If someone is absent or idle, the host can continue after the 15-second timeout.
multiplayerRoom.noEvidenceAssigned: Complete · 0/0. No evidence is assigned to you for this question. Your evidence requirement is complete; no discovery points are awarded.
multiplayerRoom.discoveryPoints: Discovery contributes +10 once per question. Shared items already discovered by a teammate satisfy your requirement; read the finding below without another click.
multiplayerRoom.findingPublished: Justified role finding published: +20. It is visible to the team below.
multiplayerRoom.unsupportedChange: Unsupported change: uptime −5%, timer −5s. Review the evidence before answering.
multiplayerRoom.compareClue: {name}: {responsibility} Compare your clue with your teammate’s before deciding.
multiplayerRoom.noDiscoveries: No discoveries yet. Unopened clues stay private.
multiplayerRoom.sharedHintAsk: Ask for a shared hint (−25 team points)
multiplayerRoom.discoverToAnswer: Discover your evidence to submit an answer.
multiplayerRoom.evidenceOutstanding: Required evidence is outstanding. The host can continue when the timeout ends.
multiplayerRoom.hostContinued: The host continued with current evidence. Missing responders can rejoin and discover their evidence; their points are not awarded automatically.
multiplayerRoom.hostMayContinue: Host may continue with current evidence in {seconds}s.
multiplayerRoom.evidenceTimeoutReached: Evidence timeout reached. The host may continue with current evidence.
multiplayerRoom.individualPoints: Correct decision: +100 individual points, once. Team points are awarded separately when the host continues.
multiplayerRoom.penaltyRemains: Uptime −5%, time −5s. Review the findings and choose a different decision above; the penalty remains.
multiplayerRoom.hostContinues: The host continues after answering and receiving teammate answers, or after choosing to continue with current evidence.
multiplayerRoom.teamOutcome: Team outcome: {outcome} · Team score {score} · Uptime {uptime}% ({uptimeScore}/1000) · Best streak {best} · Hints −{hints}
multiplayerRoom.outcomeRow: {incidentId}: {result} · {points, plural, one {# team point} other {# team points}} · {mistakes, plural, one {# mistake} other {# mistakes}} · {hints, plural, one {# hint} other {# hints}}
multiplayerRoom.reconstructionFlow: Symptoms → evidence → hypothesis → test → repair → verification. Scores record contributions, not mastery.
multiplayerRoom.noEvidenceDiscovered: No evidence was discovered for this decision.
multiplayerRoom.overriddenNote: The host used the evidence fallback.
multiplayerRoom.hintNote: The team used a shared hint (−25 points).
multiplayerRoom.contributionRow: {name}{leftRoom}: {score} total — evidence {evidence}, correct answers {answers}, useful actions {actions}, resolution {resolution}
multiplayerRoom.noMistakes: No mistakes were recorded. Use the transfer question to check understanding.
multiplayerRoom.hostStartsNext: The host starts the next incident and rotates roles.

subnetGrading.isHost: Reconsider whether the given address equals the network or broadcast boundary; neither is usable in this exercise.
subnetGrading.capacity: Capacity: use 2^(32 − prefix) − 2, reserving network and broadcast.
subnetGrading.blockSize: Block size: look at the prefix boundary in octet {octet}; use 256 minus that mask octet (256 for a full host octet).
subnetGrading.mask: Mask: the prefix is the number of leading 1 bits, followed by host 0 bits.
subnetGrading.alignField: {field}: align the network down to its block boundary; broadcast is the final address and usable addresses lie strictly between.
subnetGrading.orderRule: Use each requirement once, from largest usable count to smallest. Equal-count links can be in any order.
subnetGrading.linkPrefix: {id}: links must use /30 in this mission.
subnetGrading.insufficientSpace: Insufficient space: your chosen block sizes together exceed the parent. Reconsider oversized LANs.
subnetGrading.prefixMismatch: {id}: use the prefix you selected in the preceding step.
subnetGrading.designEnterBlock: {id}: Enter a block and its usable gateway/interface addresses.
subnetGrading.designOutOfRange: {id}: Out of range: the entire block must fit inside {parent}.
subnetGrading.designCapacity: {id}: Insufficient capacity: /{prefix} provides {capacity} usable, but {hosts} are required (gateway included).
subnetGrading.designLinkPrefix: {id}: This mission uses /30 point-to-point links, with exactly two usable interface addresses.
subnetGrading.designGatewayRange: {id}: Gateway/interface must be usable inside its block, not network or broadcast.
subnetGrading.designPeerRange: {id}: The peer interface must also be usable inside this /30.
subnetGrading.designDistinct: {id}: The two link interfaces must have distinct usable addresses.
subnetGrading.designOverlap: {id}: Overlap with {other}: two segments cannot share an address block.
subnetGrading.designParentSpace: {id}: Insufficient parent space: minimum blocks need {minimum} addresses, but the parent has {size}.

constraints.label: Capacity, alignment, disjoint blocks, containment and usable distinct interfaces; different prefixes fit requirements
constraints.explanation: A layout is valid because it meets these constraints, not because its addresses match a sample. Choosing smaller sufficient blocks conserves space; using larger blocks can still be valid if everything fits.

match.label: It matches a sample or the addresses were entered, so no boundary/interface checks are needed
match.explanation: An interaction or familiar-looking address is not proof. Check usable capacity, overlap, alignment, containment and interfaces independently.

subnetGame.intro: Detect a subnet, then design an address plan. Verify your reasoning, not just a familiar-looking answer. IPv4 with conventional network/broadcast reservations; no /31 or /32 rules in this release.
subnetGame.choosePracticeBody: Guided Practice includes formulas and coaching without a timer. Challenge asks you to solve independently; optional hints remain available. Each correct step earns 100 once, or 75 with an explicit hint. First attempts, retries, hint use and completion stay separate; points do not establish mastery.
subnetGame.practiceFootnote: Ten readable exercise headers were independently calculated. Ambiguous image strips are excluded and documented. Source IPs are arithmetic exercises, not allocations you may use on a production network. A transfer follows completion.
subnetGame.progressLine: First attempts {firstCorrect}/{attempted} ({accuracy}) · Hints {hints} · Retries {retries} · Completed {completed}/{total} · Points {points}
subnetGame.transferDone: ✓ Independent transfer completed on a new problem. Evidence from one check, not enduring mastery.
subnetGame.practiceDone: Practice completed. Feedback-assisted or familiar-problem completion is not proficiency; try a new transfer before drawing that conclusion.
subnetGame.exerciseBits: /{prefix} leaves {bits} host bits: {size} addresses, {capacity} conventional usable hosts.
subnetGame.sourceLine: Source {source} · Parent prefix not supplied: equal-size subnet count is not inferred from historical classes.
subnetGame.layoutNote: Different valid layouts are accepted. Larger sufficient LAN blocks can be valid if the full design fits, but consume more parent space. Three /30 links reserve network/broadcast and assign their two usable interface addresses.
subnetGame.hintAssistedConcept: Hint-assisted; revisit this concept without the hint.
subnetGame.noErrorsNote: No errors or hints recorded. Explain your result in words and apply it to a different problem.

mask.label: Subnet mask and block size
mask.objective: Translate an IPv4 prefix into a mask and increment

bounds.label: Network and broadcast
bounds.objective: Find the aligned network and broadcast boundaries

range.label: Usable address range
range.objective: Reserve network/broadcast and identify usable addresses

capacity.label: Usable capacity and given address
capacity.objective: Calculate usable capacity and classify a host address

objectives.order: Reserve large blocks first to avoid fragmented space
objectives.allocation: Verify alignment, disjoint blocks, containment and usable interfaces
objectives.reason: Explain how constraints verify a VLSM plan

subnetGame.missionParagraph: Parent {parent}; A/B/C/D usable counts include their gateway interfaces. Each point-to-point link requires two distinct usable router-interface addresses in a /30. No extra gateway is added to the given counts. Accept any address layout that meets these constraints.
subnetGame.givenBlock: Given {address}. Block size means the increment in boundary octet {octet} (256 for a complete host octet). Follow the stated prefix, not a class default.
subnetGame.guidance: Guidance: prefix = network bits out of 32; block size = 2^(32 − prefix); usable hosts = block size − 2. Align the network to a block boundary. For VLSM, allocate larger requirements first; a gateway uses one of the stated usable addresses.
subnetGame.reasonPrompt: What makes this a verified VLSM design?
subnetGame.guidedNote: Guided completion is supported practice, not proficiency.
subnetGame.challengeNote: An unaided transfer is needed before suggesting proficiency.
subnetGame.hintDetective: Convert prefix bits to the mask, align down to the block boundary, then reserve the first and last addresses.
subnetGame.hintArchitect: For this parent, compare each requirement to 2^h − 2. Smallest sufficient LAN prefixes: {prefixes}; use /30 links. No block may overlap or escape the parent.
subnetGame.hintGeneric: Use the IPv4 context in the source notes.
subnetGame.resetNote: Only the latest solo run is saved in this browser’s localStorage when available. No account, timer, multiplayer scoring or analytics. Reset clears this game’s saved run; Outage Ops and other progress are unaffected.
